quest.title: Truth in the Stones
quest.description: You arrive at the mine, the scene of the incident, and begin your investigation. A series of clues makes clear that there is nothing ordinary about this disappearance. What is the connection between the mysterious person behind this incident and the missing miners? Where did the missing miners disappear to? You have to know the truth.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Mora x24100, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x5

talks.objective: Head to the mining site that Uncle Dai mentioned

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, this mine is huge...

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: This is where the incident occurred.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: Six days ago, a group of us left the site to attend to other matters. When we returned, the four men we'd left behind had vanished.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: I led a team around the entire mine but found no trace. That's when I decided to enlist help.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: So four miners have disappeared.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: Yes. There were ten of us. We lost Long, Bold Cen, Brave Cen, and Mao. I worked with all of them.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Workers in this trade are usually young men in the prime of their lives. Could it be that the four of them left for another mine?

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: Unlikely. There's no other lodging for miles around, and we didn't pass any other mines on the way over.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Huh... such a huge mine. Did you really manage to explore every corner?

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: Underground, overground... we left no stone unturned. We tried everything short of digging further into the earth itself. How could four sturdy young men just vanish into the bedrock?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: We'll need to explore the site ourselves before extracting any conclusions.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: Very well, I'll wait here, please proceed wherever you'd like. If you come across any clues, let me know straight away.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Over here! What's this?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A pile of shirts, some trousers...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: A few everyday items, they must belong to Uncle Dai and his men.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: One, two, three, four...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... that seems right. Ten shirts, ten pairs of trousers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These must be spares, right? Look, Uncle Dai's clothes are identical.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: The four of them have been gone for six days without a change of clothes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's also a few handkerchiefs and some soap lying around... Oh, and some tool belts.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Items for washing one's face before the dawn shift... mining equipment...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... they didn't take any supplies...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Hmm, correct.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Improbable.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: There are four pickaxes missing. It seems likely they left with the tools of their trade.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: They had time to take their tools, but not their everyday items? Curious.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... why would someone set off with their tools, but leave their luggage behind?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: One: They were working close by and didn't need to move their personal effects. But seeing as they've yet to return, this seems an unlikely hypothesis.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Or, two: They were forced to leave and had no time to think about their supplies.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Do you think... someone kidnapped them?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: It's certainly a possibility. We'll need more clues before any further inference can be made.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If they didn't leave, maybe they were made to leave... Let's make a note and let Uncle Dai know.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kun Jun, what do you have there?

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Oh, right on time.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Did you find anything?

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: There's a chunk of ore here, perhaps there are clues within.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ore? What does it have to do with the disappearance?

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Let's find out. I'll give it a try. A moment please.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: ... Okay...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Looks like he's concentrating really hard. What's he up to?

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: I see... four men... following someone out of the mine... it looks like a child.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A child? What's a child doing in a mine!?

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: I'm not sure...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Also, how did you "see" anything exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Oh! I don't mean "see" in the traditional sense... I—I would appreciate it if what I'm about to tell you remained a secret. It's a little odd... I've never dared to tell anyone before.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: I can... perceive the memories of ore.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh—!?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: "Perceive?" So there's no... conjecture at work?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean you can put your hand on a rock and — boom! It just happens?

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: I've always sensed that ore contains "memories." Sometimes it records events that occur in the surrounding area. All I have to do is touch one and focus my attention, and the memories come to me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Amazing! So you can find out everything that ever happened there!

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: It depends on the ore. Some ores have astounding memories. Others, like Iron Ore and White Iron Ore aren't up to much. Their memories are hazy.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Cor Lapis and crystal memories are much stronger. They record more events and in greater detail.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Stone-seeing... fascinating. A rare ability indeed. It was prudent of Uncle Dai to recruit you, Mr. Kun Jun.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Haha, I'm glad I can be of assistance.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Based on what I saw, I believe they followed this path.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: This will take us north, away from the mine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: North... another clue for Uncle Dai! Let's make a note of it.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Excuse me sir, are you one of the workers here?

dialogues.speaker: Bravo
dialogues.text: Ah! Yes, yes! You must be here about the disappearance. Please find them if you can!

dialogues.speaker: Bravo
dialogues.text: I... I don't know what happened. The weather was gloomy that day, the foreman left with a few men.

dialogues.speaker: Bravo
dialogues.text: I stayed behind with the other four. After a while I decided to take a break... just to catch my breath!

dialogues.speaker: Bravo
dialogues.text: I ended up falling asleep in the shelter inside. When I woke up, there was no sight of them! I'd only just been speaking with them and suddenly... they'd vanished...

dialogues.speaker: Bravo
dialogues.text: Maybe... maybe I'm next...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: So the men that were out working disappeared, with the only one left to tell the tale having been asleep in a shelter.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Perhaps an accident occurred on-site.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... What a scary thought...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: An on-site accident... We should note that down too.

talks.objective: Report the outcome of your investigation to Uncle Dai

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: You're back! How are the investigations going?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: We found three clues in the vicinity.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: First, there are four missing pickaxes, yet everyday items are still in their place. This suggests that your men didn't leave of their own accord, but were forced to.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: Forced to!? But... who would kidnap miners?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Who, indeed. Second, there were five workers at the mine. One of them left the site to take respite. When he awoke, his colleagues had disappeared without a trace.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Those who kept working all disappeared. The one who left early emerged safe and sound. It would appear that the incident occurred on-site.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: Now that you mention it, I recall Bravo saying that he took a break.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: Could someone have entered the site and simply walked away with them!?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: This leads me to my third point. Mr. Kun Jun here made good use of his... expert techniques... to arrive at a conclusion. It was a child that took your men away.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: A child!? But there are no settlements here for miles around! There's no way a child would have made it over to the mine!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Unlikely as it sounds, that's our conclusion. Your men were following a child.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: Where did they go?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: We believe that they followed the road north, away from the mine and toward the ruins.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: North! Right, I'll rally my men and head in pursuit.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you need help?

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: You've been invaluable to the investigation, but leave the legwork to us. If we set off now and make haste, we might be able to catch them.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Not so fast. The incident occurred six days ago. Even if they set out on foot, they will have covered a lot of ground by now.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: *sigh* You're right... New plan. I'll lead my search party over to the settlements further out and make some inquiries.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: There are only a few settlements around here with lodging for the night. We'll go investigate and see if we can come up with anything.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: In the meantime you could keep looking for clues. If we don't see each other, let's reconvene at Wangshu Inn tomorrow evening.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Agreed.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: Alright, me and my men will get going!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... they're gonna talk to the people over at the settlements, while we keep investigating here...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Correct.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... there aren't any more clues at the mine... Shouldn't we go north?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Wait... I believe we're missing someone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh yeah, where's Kun Jun? Paimon bets he's still investigating. Let's go find him!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kun Jun! What are you searching for? We're all out of clues! Let's get going!

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Ah, apologies, I'm conducting a quick search for my own benefit. I'm looking for a precious stone known as Dragonfall.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Dragonfall?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Dragonfall is often used in forging. What use do you have for it?

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: I... I don't know.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: I—I'm sorry, I don't recall why I'm seeking it... I've been feeling very... absent lately. Name and address aside, I'm having trouble remembering things.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: In fact, I've been feeling extremely... anxious... as if there's something I've forgotten to finish. It's... an unpleasant sensation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon knows that feeling! When you know you've forgotten something but you can't remember exactly what it is.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Ugh... I don't even know where to start with it, I've been... aimlessly wandering. That day at the market, I overheard a conversation while I was buying something. They mentioned Dragonfall.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: It sounded so familiar to me, as if whatever it was I had to do was linked to that stone... So I decided to look for some.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Perhaps if I can retrieve some, I'll remember what it is I have to do.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I see... If I am able to during our endeavour, I will help you look for this stone.

response.speaker: Kun Jun
response.text: Really? Oh, thank you Mr. Zhongli! You're too kind!

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Think nothing of it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Shouldn't we get going?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Heading north from The Chasm, we'll reach Lingju Pass. If this is indeed the path they chose, there will be traces.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great! Let's have a look!

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: We'll work more efficiently if we split up. I'll start my investigations here.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Hmm... let's start with the details... what type of rocks do we have here...

dialogues.speaker: Observe Stone
dialogues.text: (It looks like... some sort of Cor Lapis?)

dialogues.speaker: Observe Stone
dialogues.text: (It was able to record the information we needed. A curious stone, indeed.)

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Dai
dialogues.text: I'll leave the investigations to you.

dialogues.speaker: Kun Jun
dialogues.text: Could it be that the child I saw kidnapped them? Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Bravo
dialogues.text: Where did my friends disappear to? Ugh... I tremble just thinking about it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've found some clues. Time to report back to Uncle Dai.
